title: Decoupling of the QAOA into independent spin-boson systems and high-depth performance on pure and mixed spin glasses
authors: Sami Boulebnane, Abid Khan, Pragna Subrahmanya, Dylan Herman, Edward Farhi, Benjamin Villalonga, Ruslan Shaydulin
abstract: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is regarded as a promising candidate for near-term quantum advantage in combinatorial optimization, yet our ability to study it at scale is limited. Exact recursive formulas have been introduced for predicting QAOA performance on large spin glasses, but the computational cost of evaluating them grows exponentially with the number of QAOA layers, preventing the study of QAOA in the promising high-depth regime. In this work, we show that for the task of computing QAOA energy on any mixed dense spin glass problem, spins approximately decouple into independent spin-boson systems. In the infinite-size limit, the decoupling becomes exact, establishing the spin-boson mapping as a natural framework for the many-body physics of QAOA. This generalized spin-boson mapping gives a recursive procedure for computing QAOA energies that can be executed at modest cost using tensor networks. As a numerical application, we optimize QAOA on pure and mixed spin glasses at depths intractable for prior techniques, observing that higher-degree problems require more layers for a comparable approximation ratio while angle optimization becomes more challenging. While decoupling enables the evaluations of QAOA energies at large size and depth, it does not enable strong simulation of QAOA; a quantum computer is required to sample the bitstring corresponding to the predicted energy.
summary: This work develops a generalized spin-boson mapping to overcome the exponential computational barrier in analyzing the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) on large spin glasses. By showing that the system decouples into independent spin-boson units in the infinite-size limit, the authors enable the calculation of QAOA energies at previously inaccessible depths. This provides deep theoretical insight into the scaling and limitations of quantum optimization algorithms.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of studying the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) performance on large spin glasses, especially in the high-depth regime, where exact calculations become exponentially costly.
main_result: The authors show that for mixed spin glasses, the QAOA energy calculation can be mapped onto an effective, solvable spin-boson system, allowing for recursive computation at depths previously intractable.
method: The core method involves establishing a generalized spin-boson mapping by demonstrating that spins approximately decouple into independent spin-boson systems in the thermodynamic limit, enabling the use of tensor network techniques for energy evaluation.
model_or_system: The system studied is the spin glass, modeled by a Hamiltonian involving couplings $J(q)$ and coefficients $c_q$. The analysis focuses on the QAOA circuit structure applied to these spin glass Hamiltonians.

paper_structure: The paper first establishes the spin-boson mapping for QAOA energy calculation, providing a recursive procedure. It then applies this to numerically optimize QAOA on pure and mixed spin glasses, analyzing the convergence trends as a function of spin order and depth.
why_interesting: The spin-boson mapping provides a powerful, analytically tractable framework to analyze complex, many-body quantum optimization algorithms like QAOA, connecting quantum computation performance to established models in condensed matter physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Approximate decoupling of a subset {1, 2, 3, 4} of spins in spin-glass QAOA. In the thermodynamic limit, these spins become independent, with each coupled to its own system of bosons. The evolution of each spin is described by the recursive spin-boson dynamics presented in Sec. II.

FIG. 2. Optimized QAOA on pure q-spin models. (a) Relative gap to the Parisi value, 1 −νq(p)/Πq, for the pure 4-spin model against 1/pη, with the fit νq(p) = νalg,q −c p−η (blue), whose p →∞asymptote is pinned to the algorithmic threshold (green dash-dot); c = 0.669 and η = 0.648, from the 54 points with 15 ≤p ≤80. (b) Decay exponent η (left axis) and the algorithmic threshold as a fraction of the Parisi optimum, νalg,q/Πq (right axis, dash-dot), against spin order; curve colors match their axes, which scale independently. (c) Relative gap 1 −νq/Πq at fixed depths p = 10, 20, 30, 40 (blue shades) and at the algorithmic threshold (green dash-dot).

FIG. 3. QAOA along the 2-spin to 8-spin path ξ(t) = (1 −α)t2/2 + αt8/8 (pure 2-spin at α = 0, pure 8-spin at α = 1). (a) Algorithmic threshold and optimized QAOA energy densities for different values of p. Energies are reported as the relative gap to the optimum 1 −να/Πα; each blue curve is a fixed QAOA depth p (darker is deeper), and the green curve is the algorithmic threshold νalg,α. The optimized energy exhibits points of non-differentiability (“cusp”). The rightmost cusp occurs at an increasingly higher value of α as p increases.
